disclaimer: Not an official DeepSeek standard, not a certification, not a security audit, and not a legal GB/GB-T/GB-Z instrument. The GB analogy is a communication aid only.

rules: Depth and evidence are independent; never collapse them into one score.
A skip is not a pass; not-run is not a pass; static is not runtime.
Certification grades A-D are orthogonal to these levels.

levels.label: DSH-ENTRY
levels.question: Can an existing plugin be recognized, installed, and booted without changing its code?
levels.requiredForClaim: G0-G5 at the recorded dsh/cordis versions; G4 is static, G5 is freshness

gates.check: dsh.bundle.patch parses
base + sample compose; inserted row names resolve
evaluatePluginCompatibility admits, or an explicit exact-version exemption applies
real boot(): every target row is ACTIVE or disabled
when dsh.client exists: exports['./client'] and a package-root row
report carries runtime version/commit/artifact mtime; stale evidence is marked stale

levels.label: DSH-FLOW
levels.question: Can a user install, configure, use, recover, upgrade, and uninstall the plugin without surprises?
levels.requiredForClaim: J1-J8 with recorded evidence; manual journeys are allowed but must be marked manual

gates.check: install and remove: add -> dump-config -> remove; no hand-edited profile
enable and disable: default on/off, stable id, dump diff is correct
configuration: schema/defaults, invalid value fails loudly with a field path, volatile hot change
first success: five-minute quickstart, readable error with three elements
permissions and disclosure: capabilities/labels/commitments match README, forbidden words 0
upgrade, rollback and uninstall: two versions, data preserved, rollback <=2 commands, no residue
observability: start line name@version, diagnosable failure/pending, log path
client/server shapes: headless/web/client-off work or are explicitly refused

levels.label: DSH-BOOST
levels.question: Does the plugin use Cordis primitives (effect, inject, volatile, events, seams, jobs, bounded parallelism) to make development and use measurably cheaper?
levels.claim: guiding practice; evidence cards, no badge
levels.requiredForClaim: LEV-1..LEV-8 evidence cards with environment, input, command, negative control, result, version anchor, limitations

gates.check: effects/timers/connections/watchers/subprocesses are registered as effects and return to baseline
required services are injected; optional ones use ctx.get; no polling
hot config uses volatile()/get(); config change does not remount
event modes match; waterfall observers call next(); notification listeners are isolated
seam/isolate/group used only when needed; per-agent ctx is honored
tool/prompt declarations are byte-stable; volatile data goes through systemPrompt.context
independent calls use bounded parallelism; long work uses jobs; cancellation propagates
bundle patch/preset expresses differences; every practice has an evidence card

dsh-plugin-doctor.note: Doctor maps its R/K/D/X results to an ENTRY status; it does not run J1-J8 or LEV benchmarks.

dsh-plugin-certification.note: Grade A-D is orthogonal; certification evidence is necessary but not sufficient for ENTRY runtime.

dsh-plugin-guide.note: The guide teaches the levels and routes authors to the checker/audit; it does not certify.

dsh-plugin-kit.note: Kit supplies the shared peer range and skeleton; it can carry level metadata in a future release.

dsh-test-drive.note: Test-drive is the install/load evidence source for ENTRY and certification dimension E.

dsh-score.note: Score is a quality summary; it must not label a plugin with a DSH level.

dsh-plugin-portal.note: A portal displays labels; it must not derive a level from stars or ratings.

dsh-catalog.note: A market catalog may display evidence-backed labels; no label without a link.

dsh-checkers.note: A 53-checker bundle; it feeds ENTRY static, not runtime G0-G3.

dsh-policy-ledger.note: Install-only diagnosis; maps failures to G0/G2/G3 attribution.

dsh-cert-mcp.note: Read-only MCP over the certification registry; it does not assign levels.
